Overbidding risks paying above value if competitors’ bids fall between your value and bid; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. [ Second-price, sealed-bid auction with independent private values. Dominant strategy is to bid true value: it maximizes expected profit because the bid only determines if you win, not the price you pay. Overbidding risks paying above value if you barely beat a high rival; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. No strategic signaling since only 1 round and values are independently redrawn. Therefore, bid exactly my value, $9. ]

Second-price auction with independent private values. Dominant strategy is to bid true value: maximizes expected profit and avoids overbidding risk (negative payoff if second-highest exceeds value) and underbidding risk (unnecessarily losing when second-highest is below value). With value $13, set bid at 13. No history to exploit in round 1/1. Allow tie randomization if others also bid 13; EV zero if second-highest equals 13. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 13.
